## Summary

The May 11 and November 7, 2026 [[stripe]] guides document the same minimum balance for automatic payouts. It retains funds for anticipated refunds, disputes and fees on every automatic payout schedule. Without a minimum, Stripe disburses the full available balance on the account's schedule. With a minimum, only available funds above it are paid out. If the account falls below the minimum, Stripe first tries to replenish it from available balance and uses incoming funds if none is available. The guides exclude Brazil, India and Thailand.

## Dashboard setup and changes

- Dashboard access is required for this setup path. In **Payout Settings → Minimum Balance**, enable the option, set the fixed amount and save.
- Lowering the amount releases funds into the next scheduled payout. Raising it accumulates the extra reserve from new payments. Setting it to zero or switching it off restores scheduled disbursement of the full available balance.
- Stripe generally recommends four to five times average daily processing volume, with an amount that covers typical refunds, disputes and fees. A minimum reduces negative-balance risk. Refunds exceeding the reserve can still leave a negative balance (May lines 17–47, November lines 18–48).

## Reconciliation

Report timing remains the same. The Payout Reconciliation Report shows the payout and the retained amount. In the worked USD example, Stripe initiates a 20,000 USD payout from 30,000 USD and the report shows a negative 10,000 USD retained-amount transaction. The guide says the same accounting applies in other currencies. The Balance Transaction API gives details of the hold. Report entries and payout initiation do not confirm bank arrival (May lines 49–65, November lines 50–66).

## Platforms and connected accounts

A platform sets its own minimum in the Dashboard to cover negative balances and refunds for connected accounts. For each connected account's own settings, use the account-scoped Balance Settings API and `payments.payouts.minimum_balance_by_currency` with currency amounts in minor units. Stripe recommends contacting the connected-account customer before setting it to explain why payout amounts will differ from the displayed balance (May lines 67–81, November lines 68–82).

- **Set or add.** Supply codes and amounts. Adding a currency merges it into the map and preserves existing currencies.
- **Update.** Supply the same currency code with its replacement amount.
- **Delete one.** Set that currency's value to an empty string.
- **Delete all.** Set the entire `minimum_balance_by_currency` parameter to an empty string. The example returns a null map.
- **Retrieve.** Read the Balance Settings for the selected connected account.

The May guide uses Node's `stripe.balanceSettings.update()` and `stripe.balanceSettings.retrieve()` with `stripeAccount` for set, add, update and retrieval, plus cURL for deletions. November shows cURL for these operations against `/v1/balance_settings` scoped by the `Stripe-Account` header. Both captures describe the same setting and operations (May lines 75–366, November lines 76–333).

payouts-minimum-balances-for-automatic-p.Q1: Both full captures at https://docs.stripe.com/payouts/minimum-balances-for-automatic-payouts describe automatic payouts of only the excess above an enabled minimum held for anticipated refunds, disputes and fees. Dashboard access is needed for Dashboard configuration, the reserve works for all automatic schedules, and Brazil, India and Thailand are excluded. If below the minimum, Stripe first attempts refill from available funds, then incoming funds when none are available. Lowering releases funds next scheduled payout; raising builds from incoming payments; zero or toggle-off restores normal disbursement. Very large refunds can still leave a negative balance (old raw lines 6-47 and new raw lines 7-48). Reconciliation keeps report timing and shows the retained entry. A platform can set its own reserve in the Dashboard. For each connected account's own reserve, the platform can use account-scoped Balance Settings requests to add or update minor-unit amounts by currency, delete one or all values, or retrieve the settings. Addition merges, deletion uses an empty string in the applicable field, and the clear-all response example has a null map (old raw lines 49-81 and 121-366, new raw lines 50-89 and 109-333). source-stripe-payouts-minimum-balance.md now states the above-minimum payout boundary and describes customer outreach as a Stripe recommendation. Payout initiation and reconciliation do not establish external bank arrival.
